wi_7_2_1_birthday_rocks.blurb: Birthday Rocks is a short band of quartzite on the lower east side of Devil's Lake in Baraboo Range country, perched just above the old railroad grade. The 21 climbs are almost all traditional leads, with a few set up for top-rope and the occasional boulder-style move. Most of the lines are moderate cracks and chimneys, so it suits climbers building up gear skills, but a handful of long, difficult pitches in the 5.11 to 5.12 range give strong leaders something to chase. The shorter routes sit toward one end, and a tall tower anchors the other. The walk in is quick and flat.
wi_7_2_1_birthday_rocks.approach: From the north end of the South Shore lot, take the paved path to the railroad tracks and follow them north until you reach a long electric fence on the bluff side. The rocks rise directly above that fence.

wi_red_nose_wall.blurb: Red Nose Wall is a quartzite cliff on the upper west ridge above the quarry side of the East Bluff at Devil's Lake, Wisconsin. Its 21 routes are nearly all trad leads, with one top-rope line, and they run roughly 40 to 50 feet tall. The grades climb from easy fives up to a 5.12, but the bulk of the routes land in the 5.10 to 5.11 bracket, so this is more of a stop for experienced leaders than for beginners. Faces turn toward the south and southeast. Gear is generally good, though the rock can feel damp and dusty, so give it a brush and some dry weather.

wi_bill_s_buttress.blurb: Bill's Buttress is a rippled quartzite face about halfway along the East Rampart, the long cliff band on the east side of Devil's Lake. It holds 20 climbs, mostly trad leads with a few top-ropes and a single boulder problem, running from easy fours up to the low 5.12s. A fair share of the lines fall in the 5.9 to 5.10 range, which makes it a good stop for steady leaders. The pitches are long, so bring a 60 metre rope if you plan to set a top-rope. Part of the buttress turns east, and the walk in is a real hike up through the woods.
wi_bill_s_buttress.approach: Hike the CCC trail, turn right at Pedestal Buttress, go around the top of D'Arcy's Buttress and follow the cliff top west past Tombstone Wall and Leaning Tower. Descend Leaning Tower Gully, then head east roughly 75 feet beneath the wall.

wi_08_hogleg_anchorpoint.blurb: Hogleg/Anchorpoint is a small bouldering alcove in wooded talus at the foot of the West Bluff at Devil's Lake, Wisconsin, tucked up and left of a larger boulder field and below a tower. Three main boulders hold about 20 quartzite problems, packed into a tight space so you can hop between them easily. Difficulty runs from a very easy slab through the middle grades to a few hard problems near V8, with a good spread of V3 to V5 in between. Landings are generally good. Some problems are steep and tall, so spotters and a pad are worth bringing.
wi_08_hogleg_anchorpoint.approach: Park near the South Shore boat launch and follow the dirt road west past the cottages for 5 to 10 minutes until the first big talus field opens on your left, then climb toward the tree line.

wy_poland_hill_climbs.blurb: Poland Hill is a free-standing granite hill in the Vedauwoo area of southeast Wyoming, about 8,400 feet up. Most of the 29 climbs here are traditional crack and face routes, with some boulder problems, a few bolted lines and a single aid route. Routes cluster in the moderate range, with many 5.9s and plenty of ground from 5.6 up to 5.10, while a few harder lines reach into the 5.11 to 5.12 range. The climbing faces mostly south, so it is sunny and warms up quickly. Vedauwoo rock is rough and hard on skin, so take tape.
wy_poland_hill_climbs.parking_note: Leave I-80 at the Vedauwoo Road exit, then turn onto the dirt road 700G and follow it to the parking and picnic area near the hill. The road can be rough in early spring.
